exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal delivery, planned caesarean section, unplanned caesarean section)
outcome: perinatal outcomes, infant outcomes, Apgar score, need for intubation, fetal death
cohort: The study included 23 newborns with fetal heart block, with a median gestation at birth of 37.2 weeks, followed from 2007 to 2020.
finding: Planned vaginal delivery, managed with serial fetal scalp lactates and senior clinician involvement, appears to be a safe option for selected women carrying a fetus with fetal heart block.
mod_finding: The study found that planned vaginal delivery is a safe option for selected fetuses with fetal heart block, contrasting with literature advocating caesarean birth, with all live babies in the vaginal delivery cohort having Apgar scores greater than seven at five minutes.
